newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian labour activist to be tried this week.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian labour activist to be tried this week.

text.p: The subversion trial of independent labour activist Muchtar Pakpahan will open in an Indonesian court this week, his lawyer said on Tuesday.
"The trial will begin on Thursday at 10 a.m. in the South Jakarta State Court," lawyer Lutfie Hakim told Reuters.

Hakim said Pakpahan, head of the unrecognised Indonesian Labour Welfare Union, was moved late on Monday night from a detention centre run by the attorney-general's department to the main Cipinang prison in Jakarta.
On the same day as Pakpahan's trial, three other subversion trials will begin.
Budiman Sudjatmiko, leader of the small left-wing People's Democratic Party (PRD), and four other PRD members are also scheduled to face the Central Jakarta State Court.
Subversion carries the death penalty in Indonesia.

It was not immediately clear if another two subversion trials involving an additional four PRD members, whose dossiers were lodged in the South Jakarta State Court last week at the same time as Pakpahan's case, will be heard at the same time.
All 10 men were charged with subversion in the wake of the July 27 riots in Jakarta, the worst in more than 20 years, which the government blamed on the PRD.

Hakim said Pakpahan, who was in good health, hoped he would receive a fair trial. He added that authorities seemed to be preparing to expedite the proceedings and conclude the trial as soon as possible.
"I heard they want to finish the court cases before the general elections," he said.
Indonesia goes to the polls in late May next year after a four-week official campaign period.
Marzuki Darusman, deputy chairman of Indonesia's official National Commission on Human Rights, said last week it was not clear why the men were on trial.
"One question still lingers. Why were they detained? What is the connection between their detention and the events of July 27," he said.
Three PRD activists in Surabaya, in East Java, and three in Semarang in Central Java were also expected to have dossiers on their cases handed over soon to the courts.

At least five people died in the July riots in Jakarta, which erupted after police raided the headquarters of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) and evicted supporters of ousted PDI leader Megawati Sukarnoputri.
Megawati was ejected from the post by a government-backed faction in June. Her supporters held almost daily protests for a month at party headquarters before the police raid.
Political analysts have said the government moved to sideline Megawati because it feared she would draw votes away from the ruling Golkar party at the election.
